Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-V revision: 고르는 질문 다시 묻기, the choice_retry of contract v16, with the 005-U conflict_records, the 005-T status retry, the 005-S cap and 005-R two-case paragraphs and section 6); the 005-U acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, registry shape, the expected block, mention-group and forbidden-pattern notation), the gate v17 constants and validate_suite for structure, the 005-U manifest thresholds, and evidence_registry for content_sha256 and record_problems. No implementation, run output, test, review file or other suite's expected results were read, the pipeline was not run, and all questions, records and patterns were written fresh; other suites were searched only for duplicate questions and reused names. Focus, choice questions (spec 5, 005-V): two sibling sub-codes with a choosing word and one admissible record naming both; a correct answer names the matching code with the asked value and also the other code, so the mention groups are both codes and the value: A05V-45 (ko, English evidence), A05V-62 (en), A05V-63 (vi), A05V-68 (en question, Korean reply), A05V-70 (ko), A05V-71 (vi); the matching code is the question's second code in 45, 62, 70 and 71. Choice near-misses, where the retry must not apply: A05V-58 (second code O-3 never named by the evidence), A05V-60 (two codes without a choosing word), A05V-72 (a sub-code with its own parent X-4). Kept from 005-U: conflict-template cases A05V-28, 29, 30, 44, 56, 59, 67 (28, 29, 30, 44, 67 ask what each text says); not-conflicts A05V-31, 32, 33; partial traps A05V-36, 42, 61; cap positives A05V-01, 03, 37; two-case positives A05V-16, 40, 43; role reversal A05V-14, 25, 78. Ambiguities recorded: (1) Spec 5 (005-V) does not say whether a correct first answer must name both codes; because the retry exists to add the missing code and the raw channel scores the first answer, the choice cases require both codes. (2) Spec 5 does not say whether a choice code that the evidence never names but that is a sibling of the question's parent code would trip the different-sub-code review rule; the near-miss therefore uses O-3, another family, as the never-named code. (3) 'or', 'hay' and 'nào' also occur inside other words (for, thay, nào in other phrases); the choice and near-miss questions were written so that the decision does not depend on substring matches, and no question with two codes contains 'thay'. (4) Question procedure words were kept to one per question (the change words 변경/change/thay đổi were avoided next to workplace and address words). (5) Polarity and role patterns are lexical and sentence-scoped; each was tested with a correct and a wrong answer in its language. (6) Mention groups assume the 005-S normalisation (lower case, whitespace removed).
